purpose: Sequences of NK_ LocalVar reads and the postings they must produce in euro, per PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json. Every euro figure below is net×(1+vat/100), computed and rounded to 2dp, not estimated. Vectors needing an item still listed under PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json.open_items are marked NEEDS_OPEN_ITEM and give expected behaviour only where it does not depend on the missing piece.
notation: Each vector gives the stored cursor before the read, the new read, other relevant LocalVars, and the expected result. dt is elapsed sim seconds for that update where relevant to the continuous wear formula.

vectors.covers: ordinary single action + hourly reserves, both cursor halves moving independently | restated in R2: pre-service condition added, and priced pro rata

expected_postings.note: Pro rata, the decided reading. R=1 here so the divisor is 1 and the only thing the rule does is charge for the 58 points of life the service restored, not the whole magneto.

vectors.covers: reload/crash detection — the narrower shape the pre-round-2 rule already caught
vectors.expected_behaviour: TACH below stored, MX_LOG unchanged. Reload. Post nothing. Cursor NOT advanced.

vectors.covers: reload/crash detection — the shape round-2 fix 2 added: both numbers can drop together
vectors.expected_behaviour: Both MX_LOG and TACH below stored. Reload from before a crash. Post nothing. Never reverse the V1 postings already made. Book frozen until a read shows BOTH numbers at or above (41, 1264.80) again.

vectors.covers: Reset to delivery — logged, zero billing impact
vectors.expected_behaviour: Full SPEC §2.2-2.4 seed set with MX_LOG = stored+1 (41→42). One tech-log entry: timestamp, MX_LOG 42, 'Reset to delivery — test action, not billed'. No invoice. Reserve funds untouched.

vectors.covers: new-install case — the correction in this KIT's PM review, distinguished from V3 by MX_LOG landing on 0 instead of stored+1
vectors.expected_behaviour: MX_LOG reads 0 together with the full seed set, and TACH (1246.58 once seeded) is below the stored pair. This is a new install or new machine, not a reload: log it as such, not billed. Cursor is NOT re-baselined automatically — stays at (42, 1264.80) until the pilot confirms the new baseline in the ledger UI. Until confirmed, further reads from this fresh install still evaluate against the OLD stored pair and will look like reloads (correct — that is the point of requiring confirmation).

vectors.covers: R changing between two end-of-leg reads — flag, do not guess

read.WEAR_setting_changed: REAL (1) -> x1000 (1000) somewhere in this leg, exact moment unknown from an end-of-leg read

vectors.expected_behaviour: MX_LOG jumped by 2 (rate change + tyre service both landed in this step). Hours-based postings are unaffected (never scaled by R) and post normally. The tyre service's condition-loss normalisation cannot be attributed to a single R with confidence — flag this leg 'rate changed mid-leg' for a manual check instead of pricing it automatically. price_key 'tyres' (gross 381.30) is NOT auto-posted by this vector.

vectors.covers: R = 0 — bill nothing for wear, never divide by zero, hours still accrue | R3: the F2 rounding case. 31.19, not 31.18.

expected_postings.why_this_vector_matters: The only .xx5 case in the original set, and the one figure that moves with the rounding mode. A float gives 31.18 and so does toFixed(2); the decided rule gives 31.19. K7 recorded 31.18 without stating it had used float rounding. Keep this vector.

vectors.expected_behaviour: MX_LOG unchanged (no maintenance action — consistent with Wear OFF producing no condition loss to service). TACH higher, so hourly reserves accrue as normal (never scaled by R). No wear_rate_normalisation formula is evaluated at all when R=0 — short-circuit before the divide, not a divide-by-zero caught after the fact.

vectors.covers: fuel billing source — read order matters
vectors.expected_behaviour: Billed litres = 38.4 (the FP5L_USED value read BEFORE the uplift resets it), not the typed 40 L uplift. Gross = 38.4 × 2.30 = 88.32. The typed Ramp uplift is the last fallback, after the logger burn, the aircraft burn and the tank totals — see LEG_CONTRACT.md and V19-V23. R3: the line that said nk_telemetry.py does not read FP5L_USED is retired; the B26 logger kit adds an fp5l_used datum at V274.

vectors.expected_behaviour: Detection is confirmed (SPEC §4: part at 100 = service). PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json has no 'carburettor' key yet (prices_not_yet_defined). Do not invent a price and do not silently drop the event: log it as 'service, carburettor — no price on file' for the pilot to see, and leave it unposted until a price key is added and this file's md5 changes.

strip fuel accumulation — a leg with no refuel, added per PM's second-round decision (board item ledger_fuel_in_strip: YES)
vectors.expected_behaviour: delta = 18.6 - 0.0 = 18.6, > 0. Add 18.6 to the running total. Baseline advances to 18.6 (same value, since delta was positive).

vectors.covers: strip fuel accumulation — FP5L_USED climbs, then drops to near-zero at a refuel, within the same run of confirmed reads

read_B_after_refuel.note: FP5L.js reset the counter because total sim fuel rose by more than 0.5 L in one update

expected_after_B.behaviour: delta <= 0, add NOTHING to the total (never post a negative cost) — but the baseline still advances to the current reading regardless. Skipping the baseline update here would leave it at 24.9, and the NEXT read's delta would be computed against that stale, too-high number and come out negative too, silently losing every litre burned after this refuel.

vectors.covers: a reload (detected on the main (MX_LOG,TACH) cursor) must freeze the fuel baseline too, not just refuse to subtract — distinct from V11, where the main cursor was NOT reloading and the fuel baseline still advanced
vectors.expected_behaviour: TACH below stored -> this is a reload per posting_cursor.rule_reload_or_crash. Post nothing at all this read, fuel included. Unlike V11's non-positive-delta case, the fuel baseline does NOT advance to 1.0 here — reload_safety in PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json freezes L:NK_LG_FUEL_BASELINE_L exactly like it freezes L:NK_LG_BASELINE_MXLOG/L:NK_LG_BASELINE_TACH. The book stops advancing (fuel included) until both cursor numbers pass (44, 1267.60) again.

vectors.covers: a kit rebuild changing the pinned default price must not rewrite accumulated litres — only the euro readout changes
vectors.rebuild_event: Ramp tab's live default fuel price changes (hypothetical future value used here: 2.35 EUR/L), PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json is regenerated, kit is rebuilt, sim restarts.
vectors.expected_behaviour: L:NK_LG_FUEL_L_TOTAL is untouched by the rebuild (still 50.0 L) — this is exactly why litres, not euros, are the persisted figure. Only the multiplication at display time uses the new pinned price. No litre is re-priced retroactively as if it had always cost the new rate; the strip simply always shows current_total_litres * current_pinned_price, which is what naturally changes when the pin changes.

vectors.covers: K7 gap 1. The only event that draws down the engine reserve, and the largest posting in the book. Standalone scenario, not part of the V1-V8 cursor chain.

read.note: ENG_HRS reads 0 = overhaul, SPEC section 4. TACH is NOT touched by an overhaul - it is airframe time. This is the case that makes ENG_HRS unusable as a cursor key and TACH usable. | R3, K7b F3: the overhaul action sets all seven engine parts to 100 and OIL_QT to 8 in this SAME step (HANGAR.js line 191). The plain detection table would read seven services plus a top-up plus the overhaul. This vector now carries the conditions so that reading is pinned as wrong.

expected_postings.note: vat 0, so gross = net. Not pro rata: an overhaul is a whole-unit replacement priced at its catalogue figure, not a fraction of remaining life, so the wear-rate divisor never reaches it.

expected_reserve_effect.rule: The fund is drawn to 0 and clamped there - it must never go negative. The full 35,000.00 still posts as an invoice; the 5,000.00 the fund could not cover is simply money spent. Underfunded is the realistic case and is the one pinned here.

vectors.also_pins: Reset to delivery also sets ENG_HRS (to 300, not 0) and must NOT be read as an overhaul, and must not touch the reserve - see V3. The discriminator is the value: 0 = overhaul, 300 with the full seed set = Reset.

expected_postings_F3.does_not_post: The seven parts reading 100 and OIL_QT reading 8 in this step post nothing. They are what an overhaul is, not nine separate jobs.

what_the_bug_would_have_cost.carb_str_oil: no price on file, so they would have logged rather than posted
what_the_bug_would_have_cost.why_not_K7b_s_815_49: 815.50 and 815.49 are the same money rounded in two different places. K7b summed the four exact products and rounded once at the end. The decided rule (F2) rounds ONCE PER POSTING LINE, and each of those four services would be its own line in the book, so the book would have shown 815.50. Two of the four are .xx5 cases in their own right - 415.125 and 164.205 - which makes this a third and fourth demonstration that the rounding mode is not cosmetic.

vectors.covers: K7 gap 2. The first vector where the normalisation actually divides. V1 is R=1 (divisor 1, a no-op), V6 is R=0 (short-circuits before the divide) and V5 is flagged rather than priced - so until this vector, nothing in the kit exercised the arithmetic that pick 2 is entirely about. | corrected in the pro-rata collapse: it said 50 observed points against a part that goes 35 to 100, which is 65. The figure only mattered once pro rata was chosen.

read.note: R held at x1000 for the whole step - no rate change inside it, so rule_r_changes_mid_leg does not fire and this is priced rather than flagged.

expected_postings.note: The vector the whole decision turns on: the same gauge movement at x1000 represents 1/1000th of real wear and costs 1/1000th. At R=1 this service would post 2767.50 × 0.65 = 1,798.88.

vectors.note_on_hours: Hours are never scaled by R, so the reserves accrue on the 0.10 h actually elapsed even at x1000. That asymmetry - money-per-hour real, money-per-wear normalised - is deliberate and is what keeps the two halves of the book consistent.

vectors.covers: K7b F1 and the scaled-by-R group: the rule_scaled_by_r_only group priced rather than flagged, and a definite R that divides. It no longer carries the 21 % line - see V18, which does, on a real invoice.

normalisation.group: rule_scaled_by_r_only (NK_ST_C_BRK) - loss = base * R, so the divisor is R, same as the continuous group; the two groups differ in how the loss ACCRUES, not in how it is normalised

expected_postings.note: R3: 4.02, not the 3.95 revision 2 stated. The old figure came from a gross of 1,318.21, which was the 1,089.43 net at 21 % - and that net had been derived at 23 %. The vector was never wrong about the arithmetic, only about the price it was given.
expected_postings.supplier_note: F1. The brake entry is an assumption at IAC Coimbra on Portuguese VAT now, because Claus's 2025 accounts contain no brake invoice and no Spanish maintenance invoice at all. See PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json -> prices.brakes.F1_what_changed.

vectors.covers: K7 lower-priority note: the min(R,100) cap. Also lands on the no-price-on-file behaviour, since the starter is one of the five parts with no price - so it pins the divisor choice and the flag together.

normalisation.if_the_cap_were_missed: 35.0 / 1000 = 0.035 - ten times too little. The wear model itself caps the starter at 100, so x100 and x1000 wear the starter identically; the billing divisor has to match or the two settings would not cost the same.
normalisation.cross_check: At R=100 the divisor is also 100 and the normalised loss is also 0.35 - identical cost at both settings, which is the cap working.

vectors.expected_behaviour: No posting either way. prices_not_yet_defined lists the starter as having no price on file, so per V8 this logs as "service, starter - no price on file" for the pilot and stays unposted. The normalisation above is still computed and recorded, so that when a starter price is added the divisor is already pinned and not re-derived.

vectors.covers: Replaces what V16 used to carry. V16 was the only 21 % line in the kit and the only thing that would catch a hard-coded 23 - and F1 took it away by making the brakes Portuguese. This puts the 21 % check on a real invoice out of Claus's 2025 accounts instead of an assumed price, and it happens to be a .xx5 case too, so it pins the rounding rule a second time.
vectors.source: F-BVNK_2025_Accounts_1.xlsx, row 2025-04-25, invoice 2002747740, BP Energia Espana, S.A.U., AVGAS. Printed on the invoice: net 382.50, VAT 80.33, gross 462.83.

read.note: Litres and price are the kit's LEVD figures; the invoice itself prints only the money. The point of the vector is the VAT rate and the rounding, not the litres.

expected_posting.arithmetic: 382.50 x 0.21 = 80.325 -> half-up -> 80.33. 382.50 + 80.33 = 462.83, which is the printed invoice total.
expected_posting.what_a_float_would_give: Math.round(382.50 * 1.21 * 100) / 100 = 462.83 as it happens, but (382.50 * 0.21).toFixed(2) = 80.33 and (80.325).toFixed(2) = 80.33 or 80.32 depending on the intermediate. The rule removes the question.
expected_posting.would_catch: A hard-coded 23 gives 470.48, off by 7.65 against a printed invoice.

vectors.status: The only vector in the kit checked against a figure printed on a real invoice rather than derived from the price table.

vectors.covers: Contract FBVNK_LEG/2 fuel chain, first rung. The laptop logger ran the whole leg, so burnL is the sum of the per-row fp5l_used increases and survives a refuel inside the leg.
vectors.why: The only source that is right when the tank went up mid-leg. 200 - 120 = 80 L would have been wrong by almost double, because the subtraction loses everything burnt before the uplift.

vectors.covers: Second rung. No logger run, but V274 saved the leg's own burn in its NK_LB_* logbook.
vectors.why: Same figure, weaker provenance: the aeroplane keeps only the last closed leg. Labelled so the pilot knows it did not come from the logger rows.

vectors.covers: Third rung. No burn figure at all, but the record says there was no refuel, so the tank totals can give the burn.
vectors.why: Allowed only because refuelInLeg is false. This is the rung that must never fire when it is true.

vectors.covers: Fourth rung, and the case the flag exists for. A refuel inside the leg and no burn figure: the tank totals are unusable, so the typed uplift is all that is left.
vectors.why: The rem rung MUST be skipped here. 200 - 190 = 10 L against a real burn of nearer 70: billing that would under-charge the leg by a factor of seven and nothing in the book would show it.

vectors.covers: The floor. A refuel inside the leg, no burn figure and no uplift.
vectors.why: Nothing here can say what she used, so nothing is billed and the review page says exactly that. Guessing 10 L from the tank totals would be worse than billing nothing.

r2_changes.how_the_contradiction_ended: Revision 1 of this kit contradicted itself on how a normalised loss becomes euro: the normalisation rule described one model and every vector computed the other. rounding: Round half-up on the exact decimal value, to the cent, once per posting line. Never toFixed, never Math.round on a float. Stated in full in PRICES_AND_BILLING_RULES.json -> rounding. Every figure below is computed that way, in Python Decimal, not float.
